content.comment_body: Hello all, I think I need some help with this issue. I have a pressure switch with two digital outputs. The circuit for the pressure switch is attached. I would like the digital outputs from the pressure switch to activate an output via [product_name]. So, should each digital output from the pressure switch be connected to an input of the [product_name]? In the diagram, is the 'load' actually the input of [product_name]? Which output type should be used, NPN or PNP? I'm leaning towards NPN. Experts, please assist. Thanks.

Use PNP type, then you can directly connect the switch output to the input of [product_name]. Make sure the [product_name] is powered by the same voltage as the pressure switch. If everything is 24VDC, your [product_name] should be the 24VDC version. Does your pressure switch also have a 4-20 mA output? Consider getting an [product_name] analog extension module, so you can connect that signal to your system and use it for displaying pressure, alarms (high/low), and other functions.

Thank you, I'm glad I asked. I'll purchase the PNP version. You're correct, my [product_name] supports 12/24V. I'll connect the pressure switch to the same power supply. I've already bought two digital expansion modules—planning to use the digital outputs from the pressure switch to trigger events in [product_name].

Yes, you can extend its functionality further. Use one of the inputs of [product_name] as an analog input, for example I7. You can connect it directly but you'll need a 500 Ohm resistor. Connect the analog output of the sensor to I7 or I8, and place the 500 Ohm resistor between the analog input (I7) and negative of the power supply. Then, the sensor's 4-20 mA output becomes an analog value in [product_name] (2-10 Volt). You can use that signal for both display and switching purposes.

This is helpful! I’m more curious now about analog inputs, though as a non-expert it’s a bit tough to grasp. I’m wondering what else I could use this output for—it seems important. I’ll share more updates once I start working with [product_name]—just waiting for the USB cable to arrive.
